rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Describe the requirements for effectively completing an entry-level public safety position job application.
Identify and organize their own personal history information into the various job application documents.
Identify the key personal attributes sought by public safety employers.
Identify all key components in the hiring process for a public safety career.
Discuss the role and significance of the personal history statement and background investigation.
Effectively complete the job resume and cover letter.
Identify the most common disqualifiers made by public safety job applicants.
Discuss the hiring requirements of CA Police Officer Standards and Training and other similar public safety organizations.

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Distinguish and describe characteristics of various artistic styles, forms, and works from Asian cultures.
Apply art historical concepts and vocabulary to the art of specific Asian cultures and time periods.
Describe the intersection of culture, politics, religion, the arts, and artists' roles in specific Asian cultures and time periods.
Compare the art of specific Asian cultures and time periods with other artistic traditions.

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Create and maintain a basic set of accounting records involving the use of journals, ledgers, and financial statements, emphasizing small business applications.
Analyze, interpret, and accurately record the effects of a variety of business transactions in conformity to the accounting equation and the double-entry framework.

Prepare end-of-period financial statements, including income statements, statements of owner's equity, balance sheets, and statements of cash flows, by utilizing the accounting cycle and end-of-period adjustments.
Reconcile bank and depositor records using cash journals, bank statements, and other financial information.
Process petty cash payments and adjust for cash shortages and overages.
Distinguish between employer and employee payroll taxes when calculating payroll withholding and preparing payroll records.

Analyze, interpret, and accurately record the effects of a variety of business transactions in conformity to the accounting equation and the double-entry framework using manual processes and accounting software. (Laboratory)
Reconcile bank and depositor records using cash journals, bank statements, and other financial information.(Laboratory)

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Communicate verbally in Mandarin Chinese at a basic level with clear pronunciation.
Apply the rules of basic Chinese grammar, syntax, and vocabulary to written and oral communication.
Demonstrate auditory comprehension by participating in basic oral conversations in Mandarin Chinese.
Demonstrate reading comprehension by reading basic texts in Chinese.
Write short paragraphs of 100-150 words in simplified Chinese characters and their corresponding pinyin romanization.
Describe cultures of Chinese-speaking countries.

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Describe construction job site protocols and safety standards.
Compare and contrast various trades, interactions, interdependencies, and how the basic construction process flows from one trade to another.
Apply basic construction principles and techniques across several trades, and adapt those basic skills to various construction situations.
Select specific trades to pursue.

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Identify the factors that contribute to focus and self-control in children.
Evaluate factors that contribute to the ability of young children to make connections between ideas.
Apply strategies that promote the foundations for critical thinking in young children. (Laboratory)
Implement adult-child interactions that enhance self-directed, engaged learning. (Laboratory)

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Identify the activities of engineers in the field and the office.
Describe academic pathways to degrees in engineering.
Identify the steps required to solve problems in engineering.
Identify individual engineer's role in interdisciplinary projects.
Describe a variety of software applications used by engineers.
Recognize ethical and legal requirements while engaged in engineering practice.
Develop library and internet research skills as preliminary research tools before the start of an engineering project. (Laboratory)
Use software to produce reports and carry out basic calculations and graphs. (Laboratory)
Apply Computer Aided Drafting (CAD) skills to create objects and produce working drawings. (Laboratory)
Use electrical measurement equipment such as multimeters and oscilloscopes. (Laboratory)
Apply basic computer programming skills to solve mathematical problems arising in engineering. (Laboratory)
Use computers for simple control applications. (Laboratory)
Apply rapid prototyping methods using 3D printers and laser cutters to complete projects. (Laboratory)
Perform basic operations with tools and shop equipment. (Laboratory)

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Analyze and articulate concepts such as race and racism, racialization, ethnicity, equity, ethno-centrism, eurocentrism, white supremacy, self-determination, liberation, decolonization, sovereignty, imperialism, settler colonialism, and anti-racism as analyzed in any one or more of the following: Native American Studies, African American Studies, Asian American Studies, and Latina and Latino American Studies.

Apply theory and knowledge produced by Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latina and Latino American communities to describe the critical events, histories, cultures, intellectual traditions, contributions, lived-experiences and social struggles of those groups with a particular emphasis on agency and group-affirmation.

Critically analyze the intersection of race and racism as they relate to class, gender, sexuality, religion, spirituality, national origin, immigration status, ability, tribal citizenship, sovereignty, language, and/or age in Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latina and Latino American communities.

Critically review how struggle, resistance, racial and social justice, solidarity, and liberation, as experienced and enacted by Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans and/or Latina and Latino Americans are relevant to current and structural issues such as communal, national, international, and transnational politics as, for example, in immigration, reparations, settler-colonialism, multiculturalism, language policies.

Describe and actively engage with anti-racist and anti-colonial issues and the practices and movements in Native American, African American, Asian American and/or Latina and Latino communities and a just and equitable society.

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Communicate verbally in Italian at a basic-intermediate level with clear pronunciation.
Apply the rules of basic-intermediate Italian grammar, syntax, and vocabulary to written and oral communication.
Demonstrate auditory comprehension by participating in basic-intermediate oral conversations in Italian.
Demonstrate reading comprehension by reading basic-intermediate texts originally written in Italian.
Write essays of at least 150-300 words in Italian.
Compare and contrast cultures of Italian-speaking countries.

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Perform music with metric and rhythmic accuracy as a soloist. Private lesson (laboratory by arrangement) objectives.
Perform music with technical facility using one’s instrument or voice. Private lesson (laboratory by arrangement) objectives.
Perform music with accurate intonation and/or harmonic awareness using one’s instrument or voice. Private lesson (laboratory by arrangement) objectives.
Perform music with appropriate articulation, dynamics, phrasing, and expression as a soloist. Private lesson (laboratory by arrangement) objectives.
Perform music in a manner appropriate to the style, period, and genre of the literature using one’s instrument or voice. Private lesson (laboratory by arrangement) objectives.
Perform improvised solos as applicable. Private lesson (lab by arrangement) objectives.
Practice new music from written sources. Supervised practice (laboratory by arrangement) objectives
Devise appropriate approaches to practicing music from one’s repertoire. Supervised practice (laboratory by arrangement) objectives.
Perform music from memory as appropriate.
Demonstrate coordination with one's accompanist as applicable.

rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Distinguish between personal opinion and rational or scientific theories.
Apply the basic laws of physics to everyday situations.
Use quantitative skills in applying the topics of classical physics.
